catalog_coverage.why: No prompt in this file asks Claude to write, update, or overwrite a file -- all 3 prompts read/introspect/render (repo read, self-introspection, /context).

No prompt asks the STUDENT to manually proofread Claude's output for correctness. The one verification move in the exercise ('spot-check it. Quote a specific file or function back and ask Claude to confirm it read what it claims') routes correctness-checking back through Claude, matching check_pedagogy.md §30's Claude-audits-Claude default -- not a reading-burden violation, though it lives in body prose rather than an in-fence forcing function, so it isn't itself a scored prompt.

None of the 3 prompts invite praise-shaped softening. Prompt 1 explicitly asks for candid categorization ('what's stale'); prompt 2 asks diagnostic introspection, not open praise; prompt 3 is a deterministic command render with no room for RLHF tone-softening.

No prompt sets up a multi-question STUDENT interview (the catalog pattern's shape: Claude dumping all questions at once to the student). Prompt 2's multiple sub-questions run the other direction -- the student asking Claude several things about Claude's own prior turn in one paste -- a different shape not covered by this pattern.
No prompt writes or updates a file, so no overwrite-vs-new ambiguity exists to trigger hesitation.

Both an open-ended read task (prompt 1) and a built-in slash command (prompt 3) leave room for a brief narrated opener before the substantive output; neither crosses the 4+-named-sub-step or plan-mode structural trigger in check_prompts.md §17 that would demand an explicit suppressor.
No prompt asks Claude to add a section to an existing file.
Plan mode is never invoked by any of the 3 prompts.
No prompt requests citation-bearing or sourced claims.
